title: Remark
body_md:
The above construction presents the AoI process in a general form through the
sequences of packet-generation intervals and system delays,
$(G_n,D_n)_{n=0,1,\ldots}$. In specific queueing models, however, a system is
typically specified through its stochastic primitives, such as interarrival
times, service times, and the service discipline, which induce the
sequences of generation and reception times
$(\alpha_n,\beta_n)_{n=0,1,\ldots}$. Several concrete examples of such queueing
models are presented in Section~\ref{ssec:examples}.

These particular forms are not essential for the convergence result of Theorem~\ref{thm:SGD_convergence_2}. The proof only requires that the sequences satisfy
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \gamma^{\langle k\rangle} = \infty,
\qquad
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} (\gamma^{\langle k\rangle})^2 < \infty,

$\mathbb{E}[H^4]<\infty$, 
$\lambda_{\max} \mathbb{E}[H] < 1$, and $\mathbb{E}[H^2] < K$ for some known $K < \infty$.

head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
$\lambda_{\max}\mathbb{E}[H]<1$ ensures stability of the system for all $\lambda \in [\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max}]$. Consequently, the mean AoI is well defined and continuously differentiable on $\mathcal{L}$, which establishes Assumption~\ref{ass:regularity}(i).
Assumption~\ref{ass:regularity}(ii) follows from the explicit expression \eqref{eq:psi_grad-0} of the gradient.
Theorem~\ref{thm:FD_convex} implies that the objective is strictly
convex on $\mathcal{L}$, and hence has a unique minimizer.
Since $\lambda_{\min}<\lambda_*<\lambda_{\max}$, this minimizer is
interior and therefore satisfies
\[
g(\lambda_*;\bm{\theta}_{\lambda_*})+\kappa'(\lambda_*)=0.
\]
 Thus Assumption~\ref{ass:regularity}(iii) holds. Lemma~\ref{lem:g_lip} ensures that $g$ is uniformly Lipschitz continuous on $\Theta_\epsilon$, verifying Assumption~\ref{ass:regularity}(iv). Finally, noting that 
 $\lambda_{\max} \mathbb{E}[H] < 1$ and  $\mathbb{E}[H^2] < K < \infty$ ensures 
 the existence of $\epsilon >0$ satisfying \eqref{eq:epsbound}, 
 Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_FD} establishes, under $\mathbb{E}[H^4]<\infty$, the mean squared error bound required in Assumption~\ref{ass:regularity}(v). 
 Since all parts of Assumption~\ref{ass:regularity} are satisfied, the result follows directly from Theorem~\ref{thm:SGD_convergence_2}.

label: lem:ineq
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $e^{-Y}$ is a decreasing function of $Y$, the random variables
$Y$ and $e^{-Y}$ have non-positive covariance (see, e.g., \cite{Behboodian1994}). Hence,
\[
    \mathbb{E}[Ye^{-Y}]
    \leq
    \mathbb{E}[Y]\mathbb{E}[e^{-Y}]
    \leq
    \mathbb{E}[e^{-Y}],
\]
where the last inequality follows from $\mathbb{E}[Y]\leq1$. This proves
\eqref{eq:YexpY-bound}.

To prove \eqref{eq:Y2expY-bound}, it suffices to show that
$
\mathbb{E}[(Y^2-1)e^{-Y}] \leq 0.$
Observe that
\begin{equation}
(y^2-1)e^{-y}\leq 2e^{-1}(y-1),
\qquad y\ge0.
\label{eq:linear-UB}
\end{equation}
Indeed,
\[
    \frac{(y^2-1)e^{-y}}{y-1}=(y+1)e^{-y},
\]
and the function $\gamma(y):=(y+1)e^{-y}$ is decreasing on $[0,\infty)$ since
$
\gamma'(y)=-ye^{-y}\le0.
$
Therefore,
\[
    (y+1)e^{-y}
    \begin{cases}
    \ge 2e^{-1}, & 0\le y\le1,\\
    \le 2e^{-1}, & y>1,
    \end{cases}
\]
which is equivalent to \eqref{eq:linear-UB}. Consequently,
\[
    \mathbb{E}[(Y^2-1)e^{-Y}]
    \le
    2e^{-1}\mathbb{E}[Y-1]
    =
    2e^{-1}(\mathbb{E}[Y]-1)
    \le0,
\]
thus establishing \eqref{eq:Y2expY-bound}.

label: eq:zeta-ineq-1
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Under the stability condition \eqref{eq:stability},
\[
    \lambda \mathbb{E}[B_{\mathrm{bg}}]
    =
    \lambda\frac{\mathbb{E}[H]}{1-\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}\mathbb{E}[H]}
    <1.
\]
Using \eqref{eq:zeta-by-f_B_bg}, we have 
$
\zeta(\lambda,\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}})
=
f_{B_{\mathrm{bg}}}^*(\lambda).$
Together with
\[
    f_{B_{\mathrm{bg}}}'(\lambda)
    =
    -\mathbb{E}[B_{\mathrm{bg}}e^{-\lambda B_{\mathrm{bg}}}],
    \qquad
    f_{B_{\mathrm{bg}}}''(\lambda)
    =
    \mathbb{E}[B_{\mathrm{bg}}^2e^{-\lambda B_{\mathrm{bg}}}],
\]
we obtain
\begin{align*}
\zeta(\lambda,\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}})
+\lambda\zeta'(\lambda,\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}})
&=
\mathbb{E}[e^{-\lambda B_{\mathrm{bg}}}]
-
\mathbb{E}[\lambda B_{\mathrm{bg}}e^{-\lambda B_{\mathrm{bg}}}]
\ge 0,
\\
\zeta(\lambda,\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}})
-\lambda^2\zeta''(\lambda,\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}})
&=
\mathbb{E}[e^{-\lambda B_{\mathrm{bg}}}]
-
\mathbb{E}[(\lambda B_{\mathrm{bg}})^2e^{-\lambda B_{\mathrm{bg}}}]
\ge 0.
\end{align*}
where both inequalities follow from Lemma~\ref{lem:ineq}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
{Recalling 
 $
 {\boldsymbol \theta}_\lambda\equiv (\mathbb{E}[H],\mathbb{E}[H^2],f_H^*(\lambda),f_H'(\lambda))$,
 \[
     g(\lambda;\boldsymbol{\theta})
     =
     \frac{\theta_2}{2(1-\lambda\theta_1)^2}
     -\frac{\theta_4}{\lambda\theta_3^2}
     -\frac{1}{\lambda^2\theta_3}
     +\frac{\theta_1\theta_4}{\theta_3^2}.
 \]
 Since $\Theta_\epsilon$ is compact and $\mathcal L=[\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max}]$
 with $\lambda_{\min}>0$, there exists a constant $M_\Theta<\infty$ such that
 $
 |\theta_i|\le M_\Theta$ for all $i=1,\ldots,4$ and 
 for all $\boldsymbol{\theta}\in\Theta_\epsilon$. Moreover, by construction of
 $\Theta_\epsilon$,
 \[
     1-\lambda\theta_1\ge\lambda\epsilon\ge\lambda_{\min}\epsilon,
     \qquad
     \theta_3\ge\epsilon,
 \]
 for every $\lambda\in\mathcal L$. Hence all denominators appearing in
 $g(\lambda;\boldsymbol{\theta})$ are uniformly bounded away from zero.

 The partial derivatives of $g$ with respect to ${\boldsymbol\theta}$ are
 \[
     \begin{aligned}
     \frac{\partial g}{\partial\theta_1}
     &=
     \frac{\lambda\theta_2}{(1-\lambda\theta_1)^3}
     +\frac{\theta_4}{\theta_3^2},
     &\qquad
     \frac{\partial g}{\partial\theta_2}
     &=
     \frac{1}{2(1-\lambda\theta_1)^2},
     \\[1ex]
     \frac{\partial g}{\partial\theta_3}
     &=
     \frac{2\theta_4}{\lambda\theta_3^3}
     +\frac{1}{\lambda^2\theta_3^2}
     -\frac{2\theta_1\theta_4}{\theta_3^3},
     &\qquad
     \frac{\partial g}{\partial\theta_4}
     &=
     -\frac{1}{\lambda\theta_3^2}
     +\frac{\theta_1}{\theta_3^2}.
     \end{aligned}
 \]
 Since $\lambda\in\mathcal L$, the variables $\theta_i$ are uniformly bounded on
 $\Theta_\epsilon$, and all denominators are uniformly bounded away from zero,
 each partial derivative is uniformly bounded. Therefore there exists a constant
 $C_1<\infty$ such that
 \[
     \sup_{\lambda\in\mathcal L}
     \sup_{\boldsymbol{\theta}\in\Theta_\epsilon}
     \|\nabla_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}g(\lambda;\boldsymbol{\theta})\|
     \le C_1.
 \]

 Finally, by the multivariate mean value theorem,
 \[
     |g(\lambda;\boldsymbol{\theta})
     -g(\lambda;\boldsymbol{\theta}')|
     \le
     C_1\|\boldsymbol{\theta}-\boldsymbol{\theta}'\|,
 \]
 for all $\boldsymbol{\theta},\boldsymbol{\theta}'\in\Theta_\epsilon$ and all
 $\lambda\in\mathcal L$, proving \eqref{eq:Lips}.
}

label: eq:trian
title: Proof
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since the service-time distribution is known, the functions
$\zeta(\lambda,\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}})$ and
$\zeta'(\lambda,\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}})$ are uniquely determined by
$\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}$ through the fixed-point equation
\[
    \zeta(\lambda,\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}})
    =
    f_H^*(\lambda+\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}-\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}\zeta(\lambda,\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}))
\]
and Equation \eqref{eq:zeta_lambda_prime}. Hence
$g^\circ(\lambda;\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}})$ is a continuously differentiable
function of the single parameter $\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}$.

We first establish that all denominators appearing in
$g^\circ$ are uniformly bounded away from zero. Since
$\lambda\leq\lambda_{\max}$ and
$\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}\in\Theta_\epsilon$,
\[
    \lambda+\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}
    \leq
    \lambda_{\max}
    +
    \left(\frac{1}{\mathbb{E}[H]}-\epsilon-\lambda_{\max}\right)
    =
    \frac{1}{\mathbb{E}[H]}-\epsilon.
\]
Therefore,
\[
    1-(\lambda+\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}})\mathbb{E}[H]
    \geq
    \epsilon\mathbb{E}[H]>0.
\]
Moreover, since $\lambda\geq\lambda_{\min}>0$, the factors
$\lambda$ and $\lambda^2$ are uniformly bounded away from zero.
It thus remains to consider $\zeta(\lambda,\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}})$.  
With 
$a(\lambda,\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}})
:=
\lambda+\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}-\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}\zeta(\lambda,\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}})$, we have that $0\leq\zeta\leq1$ implies that
\[
    0\leq a(\lambda,\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}})
    \leq
    \lambda+\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}
    \leq
    \frac{1}{\mathbb{E}[H]}-\epsilon .
\]
The Laplace transform $f_H^*$ is decreasing and strictly positive on
bounded intervals, and hence
\[
    \zeta(\lambda,\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}})
    =
    f_H^*(a(\lambda,\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}))
    \geq
    f_H^*\left(\frac{1}{\mathbb{E}[H]}-\epsilon\right)
    =:c_\zeta>0 .
\]
Thus $1/\zeta$ and $1/\zeta^2$ are uniformly bounded.
Furthermore, by the stability condition, the denominator in Equation \eqref{eq:zeta_lambda_prime} is uniformly
bounded away from zero, while
\[
    |f_H'(x)|
    =
    \mathbb{E}[He^{-xH}]
    \leq
    \mathbb{E}[H].
\]
Hence $\zeta'$ is uniformly bounded on
$\mathcal L\times\Theta_\epsilon$.
Similarly, by differentiating the fixed-point equation and (29) with respect to
$\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}$ and noting that
\[
    \left|f_H''(x)\right|
    = \mathbb{E}[H^2 e^{-xH}]
    \le \sup_{y \ge 0} y^2 e^{-\lambda_{\min}y}
    < \infty,
\]
 
we have that $\partial \zeta/\partial \lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}$
and $\partial \zeta'/\partial \lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}$
 
are also uniformly bounded on $\mathcal L\times\Theta_\epsilon$.
Consequently,
\[
    \sup_{\lambda\in\mathcal L}
    \sup_{\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}\in\Theta_\epsilon}
    \left|
    \frac{\partial}{\partial\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}}
    g^\circ(\lambda;\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}})
    \right|
    <\infty .
\]
Applying the mean value theorem yields a constant $C_1>0$ such that
\[
    \left|
    g^\circ(\lambda;\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}})
    -
    g^\circ(\lambda;\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}')
    \right|
    \leq
    C_1|\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}-\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}'|,
\]
for all $\lambda\in\mathcal L$ and
$\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}},\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}'\in\Theta_\epsilon$.
head: environment

label: lem:D_mixing
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(i)~Let $W_i$ denote the waiting time in the queue of tagged packet $i$. Then
    $D_i=W_i+H_i$. The sequence $(H_i)_{i\in\mathbb N}$ is i.i.d., while
    $(W_i)_{i\in\mathbb N}$ is regenerative, with regeneration epochs given
    by arrivals that find the queue empty. Hence, defining $X_i:=f(D_i,\lambda)$,
    the sequence $(X_i)_{i\in\mathbb N}$ is also regenerative, with the same
    regeneration epochs. Let $N_j$ denote the length of regeneration cycle $j$,
    and define
    \begin{align*}
    C_1&:=\left\{1, 2, \ldots, N_1\right\},\\
    C_j&:=\left\{\sum_{k=1}^{j-1}N_k+1,
    \sum_{k=1}^{j-1}N_k+2, \ldots, 
    \sum_{k=1}^{j}N_k\right\},
    \qquad j=2,3,\ldots,\\
    U_j&:=\sum_{i\in C_j}\left(X_i-\mathbb{E}_\lambda[X]\right).
    \end{align*}
    If $D_0\leq w$, then the initial workload is also bounded, since
    $W_0\leq D_0\leq w$. The distribution of the initial cycle
    $(N_1,U_1,C_1)$ may therefore depend on $D_0$, whereas the subsequent
    cycles $(N_2,U_2,C_2), (N_3,U_3,C_3),\ldots$  are i.i.d.\ and independent of the
    initial state.

    Since we assume $0 \leq f(d,\lambda) \leq1$ ($d \geq 0$), we have $0\leq X_i\leq1$ and
    $0\leq\mathbb{E}_\lambda[X]\leq1$. It then follows that
    $|U_j|\leq N_j$ and $\mathbb{E}_\lambda[U_j^2]\leq\mathbb{E}_\lambda[N_j^2]$.
    Moreover, $\mathbb{E}_\lambda[U_j]=0$ for $j=2,3,\ldots$.

    For the $n$-th observation, write $T_n$ for the index of the regeneration
    cycle containing it. Letting
     
    \[
        R_n:=\sum_{\substack{i\in C_{T_n}\\i>n}}
        \left(X_i-\mathbb{E}_\lambda[X]\right)
    \]
     
    denote the centered reward remaining until the end of that cycle, we have
    \[
        \sum_{i=1}^n\left(X_i-\mathbb{E}_\lambda[X]\right)
        =\sum_{j=1}^{T_n}U_j-R_n,
        \qquad |R_n|\leq N_{T_n}.
    \]
    For $j\geq2$, the cycle lengths $N_j$ are i.i.d.; write $N$ for their
    common distribution. Since $T_n\leq n$,
    \[
        \sum_{j=2}^{T_n}U_j
        =\sum_{j=2}^nU_j\mathbf{1}_{\{T_n\geq j\}},
        \qquad
        \{T_n\geq j\}
        =\left\{\sum_{r=1}^{j-1}N_r<n\right\}.
    \]
    Hence, $\mathbf{1}_{\{T_n\geq j\}}$ is determined by the regeneration
    cycles preceding cycle $j$. Thus, for $2\leq j<k\leq n$,
    \begin{align*}
    \mathbb{E}_\lambda\!\left[
    U_jU_k\mathbf{1}_{\{T_n\geq j\}}
    \mathbf{1}_{\{T_n\geq k\}}
    \,\middle|\,D_0=d_0\right]
    &=
    \mathbb{E}_\lambda\!\left[
    U_jU_k\mathbf{1}_{\{T_n\geq k\}}
    \,\middle|\,D_0=d_0\right]=0,
    \end{align*}
    where the first equality uses
    $\{T_n\geq k\}\subseteq\{T_n\geq j\}$. For the second equality, note that
    $\{T_n\geq k\}$ is determined by the cycles preceding cycle $k$, whereas
    $U_k$ is independent of these cycles and satisfies
    $\mathbb{E}_\lambda[U_k]=0$. Consequently,
    \[
        \mathbb{E}_\lambda\!\left[
        \left(\sum_{j=2}^{T_n}U_j\right)^2
        \,\bigg|\,D_0=d_0\right]
        =
        \sum_{j=2}^n
        \mathbb{E}_\lambda\!\left[
        U_j^2\mathbf{1}_{\{T_n\geq j\}}
        \,\middle|\,D_0=d_0\right]
        \leq(n-1)\mathbb{E}_\lambda[N^2].
    \]


    Let
    \begin{align*}
    m_w:=
    \sup_{\lambda\in\mathcal{L}}\sup_{d_0\leq w}
    \mathbb{E}_\lambda\left[N_1^2\, \Big|\, D_0=d_0\right].
    \end{align*}
    By a coupling argument, the length of an ordinary regeneration cycle is
    stochastically dominated by that of the first cycle when $W_0=w$. Hence, as $W_0\leq D_0\leq w$,
    \[
        \sup_{\lambda\in\mathcal L}\mathbb{E}_\lambda[N^2]\leq m_w.
    \]
    Furthermore, since $|R_n|\leq N_{T_n}$ and $T_n\leq n$,
    \begin{align*}
    \mathbb{E}_\lambda\!\left[R_n^2\,\middle|\,D_0=d_0\right]
    &\leq
    \mathbb{E}_\lambda\!\left[N_{T_n}^2\,\middle|\,D_0=d_0\right]\leq
    \mathbb{E}_\lambda\!\left[N_1^2\,\middle|\,D_0=d_0\right]
    +(n-1)\mathbb{E}_\lambda[N^2].
    \end{align*}
    Combining the above bounds with
    $(a-b)^2\leq2a^2+2b^2$ yields, uniformly over $\lambda\in\mathcal L$ and
    $d_0\leq w$,
    \begin{align*}
    \mathbb{E}_\lambda\!\left[
    \left|
    \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n
    \left(X_i-\mathbb{E}_\lambda[X]\right)
    \right|^2
    \,\middle|\,D_0=d_0\right]
    &\leq \frac{6m_w}{n}.
    \end{align*}
    Since $m_w<\infty$, \eqref{eq:D_mixing} follows with $K_1=6m_w$.

    \smallskip
    \noindent (ii)~Define
    \[
        Z_n(\ell):=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n f_\ell(D_i,\lambda)-\mathbb{E}_\lambda[f_\ell(D,\lambda)].
    \]
    Due to $Z_n(\ell)=Z_n(\ell_1)+\int_{\ell_1}^{\ell}Z_n'(u)\,\mathrm{d} u$, Cauchy--Schwarz gives
    \[
        \sup_{\ell\in[\ell_1,\ell_2]}|Z_n(\ell)|^2
        \leq
        2|Z_n(\ell_1)|^2+
        2(\ell_2-\ell_1)\int_{\ell_1}^{\ell_2}|Z_n'(u)|^2\,\mathrm{d} u.
    \]
    Since, by assumption, $\left|\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\ell}f_\ell(d,\lambda)\right|\leq\bar m$, dominated
    convergence gives
    \[
        Z_n'(u)
        =
        \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} u}f_u(D_i,\lambda)
        -\mathbb{E}_\lambda\!\left[\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} u}f_u(D,\lambda)\right].
    \]
    Applying part~(i) to
    $g_u(d):=(\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} u}f_u(d,\lambda)+\bar m)/(2\bar m)\in[0,1]$
    therefore yields, uniformly in $u\in[\ell_1,\ell_2]$ and
    $\lambda\in\mathcal L$,
    \[
        \mathbb{E}_\lambda\!\left[|Z_n'(u)|^2\,\middle|\,D_0=d_0\right]
        \leq\frac{4\bar m^2K_1}{n}.
    \]
    Together with part~(i) applied to $f_{\ell_1}$, this gives
    \[
        \mathbb{E}_\lambda\!\left[
        \sup_{\ell\in[\ell_1,\ell_2]}|Z_n(\ell)|^2
        \,\middle|\,D_0=d_0\right]
        \leq
        \frac{2K_1}{n}
        +\frac{8(\ell_2-\ell_1)^2\bar m^2K_1}{n},
    \]
    which completes the proof.
head: environment

label: eq:truncation_error_bound
title: Proof
body_md:
\noindent \noindent It is observed that the estimator $\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{bg}}$ is a
     $Z$-estimator truncated at zero. Define $A_0:=\{\Psi_n(0)<0\}$. We use the decomposition
     \begin{align*}
     \mathbb{E}|\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{bg}}-\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}|^2
     &=\mathbb{E}\!\left[|\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{bg}}-\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}|^2\mathbf{1}_{A_0}\right]
     +\mathbb{E}\!\left[|\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{bg}}-\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}|^2\mathbf{1}_{A_0^c}\right].
     \end{align*}
     On $A_0$, $\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{bg}}=0$. Thus the first term vanishes when
     $\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}=0$, while for $\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}>0$ it equals
     $\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}^2\mathbb{P}(A_0)$, where
     \[
         \mathbb{P}(A_0)
         =
         \mathbb{P}\!\left(
         \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n e^{-\lambda D_i}
         >1-\lambda\mathbb{E}[H]\right).
     \]
     Define $w(x):=1-(\lambda+x)\mathbb{E}[H]-\mathbb{E}[e^{-(\lambda+x)D}]$ on
     $[-\lambda,\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}]$. Then $w(-\lambda)=w(\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}})=0$,
     $w''(x)=-\mathbb{E}[D^2e^{-(\lambda+x)D}]<0$, and
     $w(0)=1-\lambda\mathbb{E}[H]-\mathbb{E}[e^{-\lambda D}]>0$. Moreover, with
     $c_0:=\tfrac{1}{2}\,{\lambda_{\min}}\inf_{\lambda\in\mathcal L}
     \mathbb{E}[D^2e^{-(\lambda+\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}})D}]$, the concavity argument gives
     $w(0)\geq c_0\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}$. Consequently,
     \[
         \mathbb{P}(A_0)
         \leq
         \mathbb{P}\!\left(
         \Bigg|
         \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n e^{-\lambda D_i}
         -\mathbb{E}[e^{-\lambda D}]
         \Bigg|>c_0\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}\right).
     \]
     Since $\mathbb{E}[H^2]<\infty$, part~(i) of Lemma~\ref{lem:D_mixing} and Chebyshev's inequality give
     \begin{equation}\label{eq:truncation_error_bound}
     \mathbb{E}\!\left[|\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{bg}}-\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}|^2\mathbf{1}_{A_0}\right]
     \leq \frac{K_1}{c_0^2n}.
     \end{equation}

     On $A_0^c$, $\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{bg}}$ is an interior solution that satisfies
     $\Psi_n(\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{bg}})=0$. For $\ell\leq\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}$, the
     concavity argument gives $|\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}-\ell|
     \leq |w(\ell;\lambda,\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}})|/c_0$, while for
     $\ell\geq\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}$, monotonicity of $w'$ gives the same bound with
     $c_1:=\inf_{\lambda\in\mathcal L}
     \{\mathbb{E}[H]-\mathbb{E}[De^{-(\lambda+\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}})D}]\}$. Thus, with
     $c:=\min\{c_0,c_1\}$,
     $|\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}-\ell|\leq c^{-1}|w(\ell;\lambda,\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}})|$
     for $\ell\in\Theta_\epsilon$. Taking $\ell=\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{bg}}$ and
     using $\Psi_n(\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{bg}})=0$ yields
     \[
         |\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{bg}}-\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}|
         \leq
         \frac{1}{c}
         \left|
         \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n e^{-(\lambda+\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{bg}})D_i}
         -\mathbb{E}[e^{-(\lambda+\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{bg}})D}]
         \right|.
     \]
     Let $f_\ell(d,\lambda)=e^{-\ell d}\in[0,1]$. By part~(ii)  of Lemma~\ref{lem:D_mixing},
     \begin{align*}
     \mathbb{E}\!\left[
     |\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{bg}}-\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}|^2\mathbf{1}_{A_0^c}
     \right]
     &\leq
     \frac{1}{c^2}
     \mathbb{E}\!\left[
     \sup_{\ell\in\Theta_\epsilon}
     \left|
     \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n e^{-(\lambda+\ell)D_i}
     -\mathbb{E}[e^{-(\lambda+\ell)D}]
     \right|^2
     \right]\leq \frac{K_2}{c^2n}.
     \end{align*}
     Combining \eqref{eq:truncation_error_bound} and the preceding bound gives
     \[
         \mathbb{E}|\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{bg}}-\lambda_{\mathrm{bg}}|^2
         \leq
         \left(
         \frac{K_1}{c_0^2}
         +\frac{K_2}{\min\{c_0,c_1\}^2}
         \right)\frac{1}{n},
     \]
     which implies the stated claim.
